newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, but seen possibly softer.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, but seen possibly softer.

text.p: Dutch money rates were stable on Monday but dealers said the undertone was somewhat friendlier which could mean that rates will come off a little.
Dealers said some market players were looking for slightly lower rates if the German repo rate was to be trimmed.

Last week Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said the German central bank could not ignore the economic signal of record German jobless figures and several dealers thought this could open the way for an easing of the repo rate in the short-term.
"This idea is still in the market," said one dealer.
The dealer added that call money rates, recently very low and volatile because of the ending of a three-month credit quota, was likely to stay near current levels.
Call was unchanged at 2.75 percent bid, but last week briefly hit a low of 1.25 percent.
Three-month deposits were stable at 2.94 percent bid.
Dealers said longer-dated deposits were the only segment to attract slight buying interest.
The guilder was stable, but still somewhat weak, against the mark at 112.33 per 100 marks.
